cases.persona: Lena in the UK, a published lender example: £10,000 over 5 years at 6.6% APR (FIN-23)
cases.situation: Lena lives in the UK (region GB). She looks at a £10,000 loan over 60 monthly payments at 6.6% APR, the representative example Tesco Bank publishes. A usual month: pay £3,000, bills £1,200 and everyday spending £800 (£480 of it on essentials), so it leaves £1,000; £1,000 is free this month. Her safety net holds £1,680, its full size. Today is 15 November 2026 and the first payment is on 15 December 2026.
cases.why: Lender quote (Tesco Bank, tescobank.com/loans, read 2026-11-12): "Representative 6.6% APR, based on a loan amount of £10,000, over 5 years, at a Fixed Annual Interest Rate of 6.4084% (nominal). This would give you a monthly repayment of £195.23 and a total amount repayable of £11,713.80." UK lenders quote an APR that already includes monthly compounding: the monthly rate r is the one where (1 + r)^12 = 1.066, r = 0.534032% (6.4084% a year, exactly the bank's nominal rate). £10,000 over 60 months at that rate is £195.2326, which the engine rounds up to £195.24 (it always rounds a payment up, so it never shows less than the lender; 1p over the quote). Today the engine reads 6.6% as 6.6% / 12 = 0.55% a month and shows £196.14, 91p a month and about £54 over the loan more than the lender. The usual month then leaves £1,000 - £195.24 = £804.76 (today £803.86). The interest is about £1,714 (17% of the amount, over the 10% line), so the answer stays "Fits only by borrowing". The fact line says the APR was read the way UK lenders quote it.
cases.plannerNote: Before 06.1-30 the engine gave: fits_by_borrowing, usualMonth 80386 (payment £196.14). With FIN-23: payment £195.24, usualMonth 80476.
cases.ownerReason: Owner, 2026-11-12 (D-26, chat popup): "FIN-23: APPROVE AP-01..AP-06 with the UK/EU reading applied ONLY when the region is set to the UK or an EU country. Pounds/euros with no region set stay as today (BR-01 unchanged)." and "Rounding up (one penny over the lender's quote) is fine."

cases.persona: Lena in the UK: £520 over 52 weekly payments at 19.9% APR (FIN-23)
cases.situation: Lena lives in the UK (region GB). She looks at a £520 laptop on 52 weekly payments at 19.9% APR, the first on 22 November 2026, a week after buying. A usual month: pay £3,000, bills £1,200 and everyday spending £800 (£480 of it on essentials), so it leaves £1,000; £1,000 is free this month. Her safety net holds £1,680, its full size. Today is 15 November 2026 and the first payment is on 15 December 2026.
cases.why: No published weekly quote was found, so this case uses the UK formula only (the APR is a yearly rate with the compounding inside: CONC App 1.2). The weekly rate r with (1 + r)^52 = 1.199 is 0.349625%. £520 over 52 weeks is £10.9540, rounded up to £10.96; about £10.96 x 52 / 12 = £47.49 a month, so the usual month leaves £1,000 - £47.49 = £952.51. This month has two payments (22 and 29 November): £1,000 - £21.92 = £978.08. The interest is about £49.92, 9.6% of the £520, under the 10% line, and 19.9% is under the 20% line, so cash would fit and the plan is not expensive: "Fits" (fits_month). Today the engine reads 19.9% / 52 a week and shows £11.05 a week, interest £54.41 (10.5%, over the line), so today's answer is "Fits, but borrowing costs more" (fits_by_borrowing, borrowing_costs_more). This is the one case where the rule changes the answer, not only the figures.
